verdict.label: BUY — Iran Peace Deal Confirmed; Hormuz Reopens June 19; All Five Regime Indicators Clearing for First Time Since February
verdict.rationale_short: Trump declared the US-Iran peace deal 'complete' on Sunday June 14, with formal signing scheduled for Switzerland on Friday June 19 — the first text-agreed, both-sides-confirmed deal in the four-month conflict. The Strait of Hormuz reopens upon signing; Trump ordered the US naval blockade removed immediately. Markets responded Sunday evening: ES futures +1.22% (~7,522), NQ futures +1.97% (~26,399). Nikkei surged 5% to an all-time record at 69,317.50; Kospi +5.7%; Stoxx 600 +1.2% at a pre-war record high. Brent fell to ~$83.5 (−3.5% from the June 12 close), placing oil $13.5 below the $97 regime trigger. DXY hit a 10-day low at ~98.8 (clearing the 100 threshold). 30Y yield, which cleared 5.00% on Friday June 13 at 4.971%, is declining further to an estimated ~4.87% pre-market. VIX, 18.90 at the June 12 close, is estimated to compress to ~16.9 — clearing the 18 trigger for the first time in this conflict cycle. All five regime indicators are simultaneously clear or clearing for the first time since February: Brent ✅, DXY ✅, 30Y ✅, VIX ✅, and SPX (futures opening above 7,460 — needs 2-session close confirmation). The June 12 night brief's explicit BUY conversion conditions — deal confirmed with Hormuz language, VIX below 17, 30Y below 4.90% — are substantively met. HOLD converts to BUY at medium conviction. Medium rather than high because: (1) formal signing is June 19 (Juneteenth — US markets CLOSED; deal response trades June 22), (2) FOMC June 16-17 is 24 hours away with Warsh's hawkish-bias risk from PPI +6.5% YoY/CPI 4.2% YoY, and (3) two-session SPX close above 7,460 not yet confirmed. The NVDA conditional add — gated since June 10 — activates today.

bear_case: Counter-argument: The Iran deal declared 'complete' by Trump on Sunday June 14 is the fifth ceasefire framework in this conflict cycle — structurally similar to the April 7, April 21, May 29, and June 11 agreements, each of which was announced with confidence and each collapsed within 48-96 hours on Iranian hardliner opposition or last-minute conditions. The formal signing is June 19 — four days away, and the same 4-7 day signing-delay window that preceded three prior framework collapses. Critically, June 19 is Juneteenth: US markets are CLOSED on signing day, meaning any deal collapse on June 19 cannot be traded until Monday June 22 — a weekend of uncertainty where positions cannot be adjusted. Brent at $83.5 already prices full Hormuz reopening; physical demining takes 4-6 weeks post-signing, so actual supply normalization lags the market by 5-7 weeks of price risk. FOMC June 16-17 is the independent domestic tail: Warsh's first meeting with PPI +6.5% YoY and CPI 4.2% YoY provides empirical grounds for a hawkish bias shift that would spike the 30Y back above 5.00% and re-breach two of the five indicators that just cleared — the regime 'all clear' is one bad dot plot away from reverting. **Invalidation: If Iran deal formally signs June 19 with Hormuz language intact AND Warsh delivers neutral FOMC communication June 17 (dot plot or no) AND SPX closes above 7,460 for two consecutive sessions, BUY conviction upgrades to HIGH at June 22 open. If deal collapses before June 19 OR Brent re-approaches $92, BUY converts immediately to STEP ASIDE. If Warsh is hawkish AND 30Y re-breaks 5.00% on June 17, BUY reverts to HOLD.**
